Practice had been a disaster, and if you asked Iven, he'd blame Coach's power trip. Not the six hours spent white-knuckling through drills while his brain looped the same ugly little reel on repeat: that name, that laugh, that stupid punchable face.

He didn't hate the guy. Hate would require caring less than he did. He just had a face built for getting hit, and a name that had wormed its way into fok's every other sentence lately, and Iven was allowed to have opinions about that. Normal opinions. Bro opinions.
So he slouched toward the dorm already mid-rant in his head, gym bag banging his hip, running purely on the hope that fifteen minutes of chaos would burn the day's rot out of his chest.
He kicked the door open, grin already loaded like a weapon.
The sentence hit a wall and died there.

The boyfriend was in the bed. Sprawled, starfished, dead to the world, shirtless, one arm hanging off the mattress like he'd been poured into it. Iven's spot. Not officially. But his, in every way that mattered, through years of squatter's rights and pure spite.
And there was a look on fok's face. Soft. Unguarded. Aimed at someone who wasn't Iven.
Something in his chest dropped and detonated at the same time, a full two seconds of pure, silent free fall before his expression violently caught up and slammed the door on all of it.
His jaw ticked. He was aware, distantly, that he was being insane about this, and completely unable to stop.
He was breathing a little too hard for a bit that was supposed to be funny.

'It's just bromance..STRICTLY', he told himself, for what felt like the four hundredth time that week, with considerably less conviction than the first three hundred and ninety-nine.'I'd do this for anyone'.
He would not, in fact, do this for anyone.
Something ugly and satisfied uncoiled in his chest at the idea of just walking over there and smacking the guy awake. I like your cut, G. Just to watch him startle. Just to see what happened.
Instead he turned to fok, and whatever had been holding his face together for the last thirty seconds finally slipped.
He looked at fok dead in the eyes then, and his voice dropped — lower, quieter, all the performance draining out of it at once.
He straightened up and let his eyes cut back to the guy sprawled on the bed, and something sharp and mocking replaced the softness immediately, like a mask snapping back into place.
He looked around the room with exaggerated interest, crouching to peer under the bed, patting at the sheets like he was searching a crime scene.
He straightened up, looked fok dead in the face, and delivered the verdict flat and merciless.
